subject: MSA + Order Form: training & output rights — proposed language
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@hightower.com>; Sam Jones <sam.jones@hightower.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form: training & output rights — proposed language

Hi Olivia / Sam —

Thanks for sending over Hightower's comments on the MSA and Order Form yesterday. We pulled together a short reconciliation of the IP and training items and suggested compromise language that preserves Hightower's data protections while allowing Redwood to operate and improve our service.

Summary of the main open points:
- Output ownership: Hightower wants a broad ownership claim on model outputs; proposed compromise narrows to customer-created prompts + attachments.
- Training / model improvement: Hightower requests a strict opt-out for any use of their inputs for model training; we propose a carveout for aggregated, de-identified telemetry and for opt-in research projects.
- Feedback license: Hightower seeks a perpetual license to feedback (to reuse improvements); we propose a time-limited, non-exclusive license for operational improvements back to Redwood with a short notice window.

I attached HF_MSA_redlines_v3.docx with inline edits and a one-page "proposed_training_carveout.txt" you can review quickly.

Ask: can you review the attached suggested language and flag anything you'd escalate to legal? If Hightower accepts the carveouts below we can turn these into final redlines for signature.

Proposed quick language highlights (very short):
- Output: "Customer retains rights to outputs that are verbatim reproductions of Customer Content (including prompts and attached files). Redwood retains rights to model outputs that are independently generated and not unique reproductions of Customer Content."
- Training: "Redwood will not use Customer Content to improve foundation models used for third-party customers except with Customer's prior written opt-in. Redwood may use aggregated telemetry and system logs for service quality and security improvements, provided no Customer-identifying data is retained."
- Feedback: "Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, revocable license to Feedback for the purpose of improving Redwood services; license terminates 90 days after Customer's notice."

If it helps, Laura (copied) and I can host a 30-min call with your counsel to walk through the compromise today.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter | Senior AE, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
Attachments: HF_MSA_redlines_v3.docx (docx, 24KB); OrderForm_Hightower_20270424.pdf (pdf, 18KB); proposed_training_carveout.txt (txt, 2KB)

From: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@hightower.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Jones <sam.jones@hightower.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: training & output rights — proposed language

Ben —

Appreciate the clear summary and the suggested language. A few quick reactions from our side after a brief run with procurement/legal:
1) Output carveout looks promising, but we need the definition of "verbatim reproduction" tightened; use cases where the model returns a small fragment extracted from Customer Content remain concerning.
2) Training carveout: Hightower wants a categorical opt-out by default for any training on Customer Content (not just foundation model exposure) unless we provide express opt-in. We understand aggregated telemetry for reliability; can you confirm what exact fields you consider "aggregated"?
3) Feedback license: time-limited license is acceptable if the termination/notice mechanism is operational (API or portal-based).

We are asking legal to propose alternate wording for "aggregated telemetry" and will share. Also, our CISO is asking for SOC 2 evidence of your telemetry storage retention timeframe. Can you loop in security for that doc?

We can do a call Monday morning PST. Which of these do you think is a legal escalation vs. procurement-level?

Olivia
Olivia Grant
Head of Procurement, Hightower AI
---
Attachment: Hightower_marked_comments.pdf (pdf, 12KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@hightower.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: training & output rights — proposed language

Ben / Laura —

Looping in my brief legal read for Olivia's questions. High level: the compromise Ben sent is a market-standard starting point. Specific responses:
- "Verbatim reproduction" — propose a measured definition: "Verbatim reproduction means outputs that reproduce a Customer Content file or prompt with >95% literal overlap or reproduce unique confidential sequences identified by Customer metadata." This gives a threshold and avoids overclaiming.
- Aggregated telemetry — define as: "system-level request metadata (timestamp, region, model ID, token counts), anonymized latency/error metrics, and non-customer-specific model performance statistics; excludes full prompt or attachment content." We can provide a short appendix describing fields and retention (suggest 30 days for raw logs, 365 days for aggregated metrics).
- Training opt-out — customer choice by default is acceptable if we can offer a clear opt-in page for customers who want to contribute data for research. However, enterprise pricing must reflect the opt-out (unit costs may be higher if we can't use customer interactions to improve models).
- Feedback license — suggest 90 days looks fine but propose an operational workflow: allow customers to toggle feedback sharing in Console (we'll include a button + API endpoint).

Action items from legal:
1) I can incorporate the wording into HF_MSA_redlines_v4 with the verbatim threshold, telemetry appendix, and explicit retention schedule.
2) Provide SOC 2 cert copy and a short security note on telemetry retention — I'll coordinate with Security.

Ben/Laura — tell me if you want me to send these as tracked changes or a clean redline.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@hightower.com>, Sam Jones <sam.jones@hightower.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: training & output rights — proposed language

Olivia / Sam —

Thanks — attached is HF_MSA_redlines_v4.docx (clean redline) which:
- Replaces "verbatim" with a >95% overlap threshold and a short citation for "unique sequences" to address edge cases.
- Adds an appendix "Telemetry and Retention" (raw logs 30 days, aggregated metrics 12 months).
- Marks the training opt-out as default; includes language about Console opt-in and a fee credit term if you opt-out (to reflect our operating economics).

We also added a short paragraph on operationalizing the feedback license: a Console toggle + API endpoint and 90-day revocation window.

If that aligns with Hightower, Karthik is ready to share the SOC 2 report and we can prepare DocuSign. If you want edits to the >95% threshold we can adjust wording (examples in the appendix).

Proposed next step: call Monday 9:00 AM PST to walk the legal team through the redline and confirm signatures. If agreed we can send DocuSign envelope same day.

Ben
Ben Carter | Senior AE, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: training & output rights — proposed language

Ben / team —

Quick update from Hightower legal & security after reviewing v4: they like the >95% approach and appendix clarity. Our CISO confirms the 30-day raw log retention is acceptable provided access controls are documented — we will take the SOC 2 evidence. Procurement accepts the Console opt-in mechanism plus the fee credit; they want the credit calculation spelled out in the Order Form (Sam will follow up).

We are comfortable moving forward to DocuSign pending: (1) SOC 2 pdf; (2) a one-line Order Form amendment that defines the fee credit calculation; (3) confirmation that the Console toggle will be available prior to the first invoice.

I'll loop in our counsel on the DocuSign once we have the SOC 2. Call Monday 9:00 AM PST is on our side.

Thanks —
Olivia
Olivia Grant | Head of Procurement, Hightower AI
